name: NVIDIA
fiscalYearEnd: Last Sunday in January (FY2025 ended January 26, 2025)
description: NVIDIA designs GPUs (graphics processing units) and related networking/system hardware, plus the CUDA software platform that runs on top of them, and sells them primarily for AI computing, gaming, professional visualization and automotive applications. It does not own fabs; TSMC manufactures the vast majority of its chips and partners handle memory, packaging and board assembly. The overwhelming majority of revenue and growth now comes from data-center AI accelerators (GPUs, networking, and full AI systems/racks) sold to cloud providers, AI labs and enterprises, with legacy PC gaming GPUs a much smaller secondary business. NVIDIA's moat combines leading-edge silicon performance with CUDA, a proprietary software/developer ecosystem that raises switching costs for AI workloads.

businessLines.name: Compute & Networking (operating segment)
businessLines.description: Data-center compute GPUs (Hopper/Blackwell architecture), networking products (InfiniBand/Ethernet, from the Mellanox acquisition), automotive AI platforms, and Jetson embedded/robotics compute.

businessLines.name: Graphics (operating segment)
businessLines.description: GeForce gaming GPUs, GeForce NOW cloud gaming, Quadro/RTX professional visualization workstation GPUs, and virtual GPU (vGPU) software for enterprise/cloud.

businessLines.name: Data Center (market platform view)
businessLines.description: Market-platform reporting cut of AI/HPC infrastructure sales — spans most of the Compute & Networking segment plus a slice of Graphics (vGPU/enterprise visualization used in data centers).

businessLines.name: Gaming (market platform view)
businessLines.description: GeForce RTX desktop/laptop GPUs and related gaming ecosystem products.

businessLines.name: Professional Visualization (market platform view)
businessLines.description: RTX-based workstation GPUs for design, media/entertainment and industrial digital-twin/Omniverse use cases.

businessLines.name: Automotive (market platform view)
businessLines.description: DRIVE platform: AI compute and software for autonomous driving and in-vehicle infotainment, sold to automakers and Tier 1 suppliers.
